title: Interactive learning product benchmark
purpose: Compare observable teaching and product capabilities, then convert verified Learning Harness gaps into implementation experiments.

dimensions.label: Structure & navigation
dimensions.question: Can a learner understand scope, location, sequence, and next action?

anchors.4: Clear curriculum, search, progress cues, and next actions

implementation.hypothesis: A course shell with concept-aware navigation will reduce orientation cost and abandonment.
implementation.direction: Compile book and concept graphs into persistent course navigation, search, prerequisites, and next/previous actions.
acceptance: A learner can locate the current concept and prerequisite path
Search reaches lessons, concepts, and sources
Every lesson exposes a deterministic next action

dimensions.label: Explanation & pacing
dimensions.question: Does the content build a mental model through motivating questions, progressive disclosure, and manageable steps?

anchors.4: Question-driven causal progression with excellent compression

implementation.hypothesis: Question-driven causal pacing will improve mental-model formation without increasing lesson length.
implementation.direction: Add pacing gates for motivating failure, causal spine, representation change, prediction, and transfer; benchmark section density and reading time.
acceptance: Each section answers one explicit learner question
Terminology follows the causal model
Human reviewers rate pacing at least strong

dimensions.label: Visual models
dimensions.question: Do diagrams and visualizations form an explanatory argument rather than decorate prose?

anchors.4: Dense semantic visual sequence tied to the explanation

implementation.hypothesis: A broader semantic visual grammar will let generated lessons explain more mechanisms without screenshots or arbitrary code.
implementation.direction: Add declarative timeline, causal graph, state machine, parameter plot, and annotated-code primitives with static fallbacks.
acceptance: Every visual states the relationship it explains
All visuals have text equivalents
Primitive contracts pass narrow-screen and keyboard tests

dimensions.label: Interactive learning
dimensions.question: Can the learner manipulate an explanatory variable and observe a meaningful result?

anchors.4: Manipulation is central, inspectable, and reproducible

implementation.hypothesis: Prediction-linked manipulation will outperform passive figures on transfer questions.
implementation.direction: Require simulator hypotheses, expected relationships, prediction-before-change, state coverage, and deterministic outcome functions.
acceptance: Controls change the declared relationship
Learners predict before reveal
Static fallback preserves the explanation

dimensions.label: Active assessment
dimensions.question: Does the experience elicit prediction, retrieval, misconception diagnosis, and transfer?

anchors.4: Aligned prediction, diagnostic feedback, retrieval, and transfer

implementation.hypothesis: Objective-aligned diagnostic checks will improve correction and transfer compared with completion-only signals.
implementation.direction: Add pre-check, mastery, delayed retrieval, and transfer contracts linked to concept IDs and misconceptions.
acceptance: Every core objective has observable learner evidence
Incorrect options diagnose named misconceptions
Transfer is assessed outside the worked example

dimensions.label: Evidence & trust
dimensions.question: Can learners distinguish sourced facts, inference, disagreement, and illustration at the point of use?

anchors.4: Claim-level provenance and epistemic status are inspectable

implementation.hypothesis: Inline claim provenance will increase trust calibration and reduce accidental overclaiming.
implementation.direction: Compile evidence claim IDs and exact locators into inline trust affordances and a source inspector.
acceptance: Material claims resolve to exact evidence locators
Inference and illustration are visibly distinct
Citation verification blocks invented or unsupported claims

dimensions.label: Reproducibility
dimensions.question: Can an advanced learner inspect or reproduce the content, visual, or underlying work?

anchors.4: Versioned source artifacts and reproducible execution

implementation.hypothesis: Exportable evidence and interaction artifacts will make generated instruction more trustworthy and extensible.
implementation.direction: Expose versioned lesson JSON, evidence packs, calculation definitions, and optional notebooks without leaking private inputs.
acceptance: Every published lesson identifies its artifact version
Public evidence packs omit secrets and copyrighted source dumps
Interactive results can be reproduced from declared inputs

dimensions.label: Learner continuity
dimensions.question: Does the product preserve progress, context, notes, and a clear return path?

anchors.4: Progress, notes, resume state, and next action work together

implementation.hypothesis: Local-first progress and resume cues will improve multi-session completion without requiring an account.
implementation.direction: Add versioned local progress, section mastery, notes export, and explicit resume state before any hosted account system.
acceptance: Progress survives reload without authentication
Content-version changes do not silently preserve invalid mastery
Learners can export and delete their local state

dimensions.label: Accessibility
dimensions.question: Can learners use the full experience with keyboard, assistive technology, reduced motion, and narrow screens?

anchors.4: WCAG 2.2 AA evidence plus manual assistive-technology review

implementation.hypothesis: Primitive-level accessibility contracts will prevent generated content from reintroducing barriers.
implementation.direction: Add browser, automated accessibility, keyboard, reduced-motion, zoom, and scheduled screen-reader gates per primitive.
acceptance: Automated WCAG checks pass on every primitive state
Keyboard and focus behavior pass browser tests
A manual screen-reader review is recorded for releases
